input: Arrange a will reading meeting with my siblings

keyUnknowns.whyItMatters: Whether a solicitor, lawyer, or executor needs to be present determines how formal the meeting must be and who is responsible for coordinating it.
The location — in-person at a law firm, a family home, or virtually — changes the logistics and what needs to be arranged.
How many siblings are involved and where they are based affects scheduling complexity and travel or tech requirements.
Whether the user is organising the meeting themselves or delegating to a solicitor or executor changes what actions they need to take.
The urgency or target date for the meeting affects how quickly invitations, venue, and legal arrangements must be made.
The desired tone — formal legal proceeding vs. informal family discussion — shapes the format, who speaks, and how the meeting is structured.
Knowing what a successful outcome looks like (e.g., all siblings informed, legal formalities completed, disputes avoided) guides what needs to be prepared in advance.

gold.taskTitle: Arrange a will reading meeting with siblings
gold.taskDescription: Organise a meeting where the user and their siblings gather to hear or discuss the contents of a will.

questions.title: Will a solicitor or executor be present at the meeting?
questions.description: Determine whether a legal professional or appointed executor needs to attend, which affects the formality and coordination required.

questions.title: Where should the meeting take place — home, law firm, or online?
questions.description: Clarify the preferred venue or format, as this drives the booking and setup tasks needed.

questions.title: How many siblings are involved, and are any located remotely?
questions.description: Understanding the number of attendees and their locations reveals scheduling complexity and whether travel or virtual tools are needed.

questions.title: Are you organising this yourself or coordinating with a solicitor?
questions.description: Knowing who is driving the arrangement determines what the user personally needs to do versus delegate.

questions.title: Do you have a target date or deadline for this meeting?
questions.description: A target date sets the urgency and dictates how quickly outreach to siblings and any legal parties must happen.

questions.title: Should this be a formal legal reading or an informal family discussion?
questions.description: The desired tone shapes the structure of the meeting, who leads it, and what materials need to be prepared.

questions.title: What does a successful meeting look like when it is over?
questions.description: Defining the intended outcome — such as all parties informed, documents signed, or questions resolved — guides preparation and agenda-setting.
